text:
alice-support: FYI customer reported a sudden p95/p99 regression in eu-west-3 since our kernel backport window overnight. p95 went from ~180ms to ~420ms for text-gen endpoints. They see occasional 504s and timeouts. Request ids: rq_eu_33a1, rq_eu_33a2.

Eve-customer: yeah, started ~2026-03-15T02:40Z during your maintenance. Traffic pattern is normal for us, no large payload changes. We can share a sample trace if useful. :frowning_face:

bob-eng-runtime: Looking at traces from the faulty timeframe — majority of extra tail latency is in "disk read" while populating KV cache. Calls to read kvpage show wait on blk_mq. Aggregate I/O wait up ~4-5x. No obvious CPU saturation.

alice-support: attached logs from customer and sample span id span_9f1. Also noticed slight uptick in 429s when retry logic kicks in.

carla-eng-infra: We rolled the kernel backport (6.2.x writeback/coalesce patch) to eu-west-3 at 02:32 UTC. Could be interaction with NVMe queue limits + new coalescing heuristics. We'll check host metrics.

deploy-bot: deploy "host-kernel-backport-euw3" finished on pool-euw3 at 2026-03-15T02:32:18Z by carla-eng-infra.

dan-eng-sre: Quick mitigation plan: 1) drain and reprovision a small node pool without the backport and route a sample of customer traffic to it. 2) temporarily increase autoscale headroom on dedicated GPUs for the affected tenants. 3) add routing override for the affected request IDs to avoid eu-west-3.

bob-eng-runtime: For a quick repro on a host node: run fio stress against nvme to reproduce I/O latency seen by runtime, then run our kvcache warmup harness. Example commands:

```\nfio --name=randread --ioengine=libaio --direct=1 --bs=128k --size=4G --numjobs=4 --runtime=60 --time_based --iodepth=32 --rw=randread --filename=/dev/nvme0n1\n# then run the kvcache warmup: /opt/redwood/bin/kv_warmup --backfill --workers=8 --profile=short\n```

bob-eng-runtime: If fio shows tail >50ms and kv_warmup triggers bursts of reads, that's consistent with customer traces.

carla-eng-infra: Quick host-level checks I'm running now: blk_mq queue depth (/sys/block/nvme0n1/queue/nr_requests), vm.dirty_bytes/dirty_ratio, and nvme firmware version. I'm also toggling writeback parameters: `echo 50000000 > /proc/sys/vm/dirty_bytes` then monitor.

alice-support: Customer confirmed they can be routed off eu-west-3 for now. They asked about ETA for fix or rollback.

dan-eng-sre: Immediate temp mitigations applied: routing override + scaled GPU pool up by 2 nodes for affected customers. Also created a small canary node pool using previous kernel package and pinned routing for a subset of traffic. Early canary p95 looks back to baseline.

carla-eng-infra: Next steps: 1) bisect the kernel patch set (we suspect writeback coalescing change). 2) test NVMe firmware candidate in lab with same backport. 3) if reproduces, either revert backport or tune vm/blk params and roll a hotfix.

bob-eng-runtime: Also adding a short-term runtime guard to avoid synchronous KV-populate on cold tails >50 tokens — convert to async warmup with soft time budget so we don't amplify I/O stalls into request tail. Patch will be small and can be canaried in eu-west-1 first.

Eve-customer: thanks for the fast response, routing away helped. Keep us posted on rollback ETA, we may schedule a brief maintenance if needed.

alice-support: filing incident doc and tagging for postmortem after stability. Action items assigned: carla (kernel bisect), bob (runtime guard PR), dan (routing/scale follow-up). I'll update customer channel with current mitigations. :thumbsup:

carla-eng-infra: quick paste of host log snippet showing stalls:```\n[ 02:34:12.123 ] nvme0n1: rq: tail lat 128ms qdepth 512 -> io_wait\n[ 02:34:12.456 ] blk_mq_run_hw_queues: queue busy, latency spike\n[ 02:34:13.789 ] writeback: background writeback took 322ms, started by pid 3421\n```

dan-eng-sre: I'll keep the routing override for 6 hours and monitor. If canary remains stable we can either revert the backport or ship the runtime guard + blk tuning as a combined mitigation.

alice-support: thanks all, updating incident channel and customer.
